summary.title: Enhanced sensitivity to variation of me/mp in molecular spectra
summary.authors: D. DeMille, S. Sainis, J. Sage, T. Bergeman, S. Kotochigova, and E. Tiesinga
summary.executive_summary: This paper proposes a novel laboratory experiment to detect potential spatial or temporal variations in the electron-to-proton mass ratio, µ ≡ me/mp. The authors argue that while variations in the fine structure constant α have been extensively studied, theoretical models suggest µ variations could be larger by a factor of ~30. The study identifies a specific mechanism in diatomic molecules where the energy splitting between nearly-degenerate vibrational levels from overlapping electronic potentials is highly sensitive to µ. Specifically, they focus on the Cs2 molecule, demonstrating a near-degeneracy between a deeply bound level of the a3Σ+u state and a level of the X1Σ+g ground state. By utilizing ultracold Cs2 molecules, which allow for extremely narrow spectral lines (Γ ~ 1 Hz), the proposed measurement could achieve a sensitivity to fractional changes in µ of δ(∆µ/µ) ~ 10^-17 within a single day of integration. The paper includes experimental spectroscopic data confirming the existence of this near-degeneracy in Cs2, validating the theoretical predictions. The authors conclude that this system offers a promising avenue for high-precision tests of fundamental physics, potentially surpassing the sensitivity of current atomic clock comparisons.

claims.description: Molecular vibrational levels in Cs2 offer enhanced sensitivity to µ variation compared to atomic transitions.
The near-degeneracy between a3Σ+u and X1Σ+g states in Cs2 is experimentally verified.

judge_context:
Executive Summary
This paper proposes a novel laboratory experiment to detect potential spatial or temporal variations in the electron-to-proton mass ratio, µ ≡ me/mp. The authors argue that while variations in the fine structure constant α have been extensively studied, theoretical models suggest µ variations could be larger by a factor of ~30. The study identifies a specific mechanism in diatomic molecules where the energy splitting between nearly-degenerate vibrational levels from overlapping electronic potentials is highly sensitive to µ. Specifically, they focus on the Cs2 molecule, demonstrating a near-degeneracy between a deeply bound level of the a3Σ+u state and a level of the X1Σ+g ground state. By utilizing ultracold Cs2 molecules, which allow for extremely narrow spectral lines (Γ ~ 1 Hz), the proposed measurement could achieve a sensitivity to fractional changes in µ of δ(∆µ/µ) ~ 10^-17 within a single day of integration. The paper includes experimental spectroscopic data confirming the existence of this near-degeneracy in Cs2, validating the theoretical predictions. The authors conclude that this system offers a promising avenue for high-precision tests of fundamental physics, potentially surpassing the sensitivity of current atomic clock comparisons.

Research Context
Fundamental constants may vary due to string-inspired models. Variations in µ are theoretically predicted to be larger than α. Cosmological measurements are limited by systematic errors. Molecular vibrational levels offer a new laboratory probe.

Research Question And Hypothesis
Can molecular spectra detect µ variation more sensitively than atomic clocks? Do near-degenerate levels exist in Cs2 with enhanced µ sensitivity? Can the splitting be measured to detect ∆µ/µ ≲ 10^-17? Is the sensitivity maximized at intermediate vibrational excitation?

Methodological Details
The study focuses on the Cs2 diatomic molecule. Two overlapping potentials are utilized: X1Σ+g and a3Σ+u. Ultracold Cs atoms are trapped at T ~ 100 µK. Atoms are optically pumped to the 6s1/2 F = mF = 4 state. Photoassociation excites atoms to the (2)0−g potential. A probe laser searches for resonances with the a3Σ+u levels. Ion yield is monitored to detect resonant dips. Binding energies are reported relative to the hyperfine barycenter. Global fits include SO2 interaction and use Hannover analytic form. The r.m.s. deviation for binding energies was ~200 MHz.

Procedures And Architectures
Energy sensitivity is defined as ∂µE ≡ ∂E/∂(lnµ). The WKB quantization condition approximates vibrational energies. Sensitivity is enhanced by the density of states ρ(Ev). Near-degeneracy occurs when potentials X and Y overlap. The splitting ℱ retains large sensitivity if one level is near dissociation. HF mixing induces magnetic dipole transitions between states. Spin-orbit effects induce electric dipole transitions. A linewidth of Γ ~ 1 Hz is achievable with ultracold molecules. Integration time of one day yields δℱ ~ 5 × 10^-5 Hz.

Key Results
A near-degeneracy was found between va=37 and vX=138 levels. The splitting ℱ is approximately 6.3 GHz for the magnetic dipole transition. The splitting ℱ is approximately 9.8 GHz for the electric dipole transition. The transition amplitude M is ~0.1 µB for the magnetic dipole case. The transition amplitude M is ~0.04 µB for the electric dipole case. The predicted sensitivity is δ(∆µ/µ) ~ 10^-17. This requires δℱ/ℱ ~ 10^-14, less than atomic clocks. The r.m.s. deviation for sublevel splittings was ~90 MHz.

Interpretation And Theoretical Implications
The mechanism relies on the density of states near dissociation. Intermediate vibrational levels maximize the sensitivity ∂µEv. Overlapping potentials allow for large relative shifts ∂µℱ/ℱ. Cs2 is ideal due to long radiative lifetimes and high density of states. The proposed method surpasses current atomic clock accuracy.

Contradictions And Limitations
HF mixing reduces the sensitivity for the directly observed X state sublevel. The study notes similar ideas were explored in other systems during preparation. Absolute binding energy fit uncertainty is ~200 MHz. Some near-degeneracies await further data for confirmation.

Claims
Molecular vibrational levels in Cs2 offer enhanced sensitivity to µ variation compared to atomic transitions. Energy sensitivity is enhanced by the density of states. Relative shifts are large for overlapping potentials. Cs2 levels have long lifetimes enabling narrow lines. HF mixing reduces sensitivity for specific observed sublevels. Sensitivity of 10^-17 is achievable in one day.
The near-degeneracy between a3Σ+u and X1Σ+g states in Cs2 is experimentally verified. Data shows lines for va=37 and vX=138. The splitting is ~6.3 GHz.  This validates the theoretical prediction for the experiment.

Data And Code Availability
Details of the data and the fit will be given elsewhere.

Robustness And Ablation Notes
Global fits account for SO2 interaction and use Hannover form.

Key Figures Tables
Fig. 1 shows energy sensitivity vs. binding energy for X and a states. Fig. 2 shows data indicating degeneracy between va=37 and vX=138.

Three Takeaways
1. The core contribution is the proposal of a molecular clock for µ variation. 2. The strongest evidence is the experimental verification of the near-degeneracy. 3. The future path involves using ultracold Cs2 to achieve 10^-17 sensitivity.
